\section{Minimum-spill lifting}
\label{sec:spill}

We now reverse the forward map from links to a centered star.  The construction
is useful on any finite oriented two-complex.  Fix a link $\ell$ incident on
$m$ plaquettes, orient those rows by $O_\ell$, and let
\[
 R_\ell=C_mO_\ell S_\ell d_1,
 \qquad B_\ell=E_\ell d_1,
\]
where $E_\ell$ selects all plaquettes outside the star.  For a realizable
centered star displacement $y\in\im R_\ell$, set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spill-form}
 h_\ell(y)=\min\left\{\norm{B_\ell x}^2:R_\ell x=y\right\}.
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Minimum-spill form]
\label{prop:general-spill}
The function $h_\ell$ is a positive semidefinite quadratic form on
$\im R_\ell$.  Moreover,
\[
 h_\ell(y)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there exists }x\text{ with }R_\ell x=y\text{ and }B_\ell x=0.
\]
Its matrix is invariant, up to isometry, under automorphisms of the oriented
complex carrying one rooted link star to another.
\end{proposition}

Thus $\ker h_\ell$ is exactly the space of star operations that lift without
external curvature.  Positive definiteness is an anti-locality statement:
every nontrivial centered operation leaks out of the selected star.

For the test block, identify the centered six-dimensional star space with
$\R^5$ using
\[
 Z=\begin{pmatrix}I_5\\-\mathbf1^\mathsf T\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad y=Zu,
 \qquad \norm y^2=u^\mathsf TGu,
 \qquad G=Z^\mathsf TZ=I_5+\mathbf1\mathbf1^\mathsf T.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Exact spillover spectrum]
\label{thm:spill-spectrum}
For every interior link of the open side-two four-cube, the minimum-spill form
is positive definite and has generalized spectrum, relative to $G$,
\[
 \operatorname{spec}_G(h_\ell)=
 \left\{
 \frac{37}{33},\frac{37}{33},\frac{37}{33},
 \frac{391}{239},\frac{391}{239}
 \right\}.
\]
In particular,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spill-lower}
 h_\ell(y)\ge\frac{37}{33}\norm y^2
 \qquad (\mathbf1^\mathsf Ty=0).
\end{equation}
There is no nonzero centered star displacement with an external-flat lift.
\end{theorem}

The theorem minimizes over variations of all $216$ links.  The central link
may be removed without changing the answer: after the incident rows are
oriented, its star column is $\mathbf1$ and is killed by $C_6$, while its
external column vanishes.  Hence the obstruction is not an artifact of
freezing the link around which the star was defined.

The strict inequality in \eqref{eq:spill-lower} should not be read as a
prohibition on smoothing.  A coordinated update may still lower total action,
and a pre-existing external field can contribute favorable cross terms.  What
is ruled out is the representation-level idealization in which relative
staple curvature contracts while all other plaquettes remain unchanged.
